004845: 
004846:    The type is *copied* first, always, even when the declarator built it: a
004847:    declarator that merely names an existing type -- `typedef int raised
004848:    __attribute__((aligned(16)));` names the one builtin `int` -- would
004849:    otherwise realign every other declaration in the translation unit written
004850:    with that type.  This is the anti-infection guard
004851:    c_parse_noreturn_candidate_function_type applies to the noreturn marker,
004852:    taken one step further: the copy is unconditional because the layout engines
004853:    want one place to read the natural alignment from, and pointing every
004854:    aligned alias at the type it aliases gives them that.
004855: 
004856:    The copy carries `has_unqualified_type`, which is what makes the alias
004857:    behave as a variant of the original everywhere else: type compatibility
004858:    strips back to the same unqualified type, and both layout engines already
004859:    have an alias branch to hang the replaced alignment off.  A request that
004860:    cannot be recorded leaves the type as it was, which is the alignment the
004861:    declaration had before this ran. */
004862: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL CTypeId c_parse_add_type_alignment(CParseResult* result, CTypeId type, u32 alignment_start, u32 alignment_count)
004863: {
004864:     if (!result || !alignment_count || type.value >= result->type_count)
004865:     {
004866:         return type;
004867:     }
004868:     if (!c_parse_reserve_type_alignment(result))
004869:     {
004870:         return type;
004871:     }
004872:     CType alias = result->types[type.value];
004873:     alias.unqualified_type = alias.has_unqualified_type ? alias.unqualified_type : type;
004874:     alias.has_unqualified_type = true;
004875:     CTypeId aligned = c_parse_add_type(result, alias);
004876:     if (aligned.value == C_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
004877:     {
004878:         return type;
004879:     }
004880:     result->type_alignments[result->type_alignment_count++] = (CTypeAlignment){
004881:         .type_index = aligned.value,
004882:         .alignment_start = alignment_start,
004883:         .alignment_count = alignment_count,
004884:     };
004885: 
004886:     return aligned;
004887: }

006040: /* Whether adding `_Atomic` to `base` takes an alignment request `base` carries
006041:    away from the type the step builds.  It is the one place the two reference
006042:    compilers disagree: Clang treats `_Atomic T` as *constructing* a type rather
006043:    than qualifying one, so `typedef int cache_line __attribute__((aligned(64)))`
006044:    gives `_Atomic cache_line` the alignment an atomic of that width gets (4),
006045:    while GCC keeps the alias's 64.  Clang is this repository's oracle, and it
006046:    is also the answer this frontend already gave through a typedef of the
006047:    atomic type.  `_Atomic` written on a type that is *already* atomic keeps the
006048:    request in both references, which is why the test is on the step rather than
006049:    on the result.
006050: 
006051:    Two places build that type and both ask here, because one type answering two
006052:    alignments depending on how it is spelled is what #726 was:
006053:    c_parse_add_qualified_type below builds the copy a declaration makes, and
006054:    c_ir_type_name_prefix in c_gen.c resolves the type name an expression
006055:    spells, which builds no C type at all and answered with the alias's own
006056:    number.  The empty table is the guard, so a translation unit without an
006057:    aligned typedef -- almost every one -- pays one compare. */
006058: BUSTER_C_SHARED bool c_parse_atomic_drops_type_alignment(CParseResult const* result, CTypeId base, bool adds_atomic)
006059: {
006060:     bool drops = false;
===== line 6103 =====
006073:    from, and it is also why the alignment record -- keyed on the alias -- did
006074:    not describe the copy: `const cache_line` answered `_Alignof` 4 where Clang
006075:    and GCC answer 64, in every position and with no diagnostic (#714).  The
006076:    copy therefore inherits the record, which states an alignment the *type*
006077:    carries and a qualifier cannot take away.  The guard is the empty table, so
006078:    a translation unit without an aligned typedef -- almost every one -- pays
006079:    one compare per qualified type. */

006107:                 .type_index = qualified_id.value,
006108:                 .alignment_start = alignment_start,
006109:                 .alignment_count = alignment_count,
006110:             };
006111:         }
006112:     }
006113: 
006114:     return qualified_id;
006115: }

006653: // How many parent links separate `scope` from `candidate`, or UINT32_MAX when

006670:             return distance;

009221: // One parameter list has been scanned to its closing parenthesis.  The name's
009222: // own list is scanned first but applied last -- it is the outermost derivation
009223: // of `void (*getf(int))(void)` -- so it only records its range here and hands
009224: // the frame on to the outer suffix; the outer list is the return type and
009225: // becomes a function type immediately.
009226: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL void c_type_parse_parenthesized_list_complete(CTypeParseFrame* frame, CParseResult* result, CPreprocessResult preprocess, u32 list_close)
009227: {
009228:     if (frame->scanning_inner_parameters)
009229:     {
009230:         frame->inner_parameter_start = frame->parameter_start;
009231:         frame->inner_parameter_count = frame->written_parameter_count;
009232:         frame->inner_variadic = frame->variadic;
009233:         frame->inner_unprototyped = c_parse_parameter_list_unprototyped(preprocess, list_close);
009234:         frame->has_inner_parameters = true;
009235:         frame->scanning_inner_parameters = false;
009236:         frame->variadic = false;
009237:         c_type_parse_parenthesized_suffix_begin(frame, result, preprocess);
009238:         return;
009239:     }
009240:     frame->index = list_close + 1;
009241:     frame->type = c_parse_add_type(result, (CType){
009242:                                              .element_type = C_TYPE_ID_INVALID,
009243:                                              .return_type = frame->type,
009244:                                              .array_bound = C_ARRAY_BOUND_INVALID,
009245:                                              .parameter_start = frame->parameter_start,
009246:                                              .parameter_count = frame->written_parameter_count,
009247:                                              .kind = C_TYPE_FUNCTION,
009248:                                              .is_variadic = frame->variadic,
009249:                                              .is_unprototyped = c_parse_parameter_list_unprototyped(preprocess, list_close),
009250:                                          });
009251:     frame->has_function_suffix = true;
009252:     frame->stage = C_TYPE_PARSE_STAGE_FINISH;
009253: }

017192:             .declaration_index = result.declaration_count - 1,
017193:             .declaration_token_plus_one = declaration_name_token < token_count ? declaration_name_token + 1 : 0,
017194:             .alignment_start = declaration->alignment_start,
017195:             .alignment_count = declaration->alignment_count,
017196:             .kind = kind == C_DECLARATION_FUNCTION  ? C_ENTITY_FUNCTION
017197:                     : kind == C_DECLARATION_TYPEDEF ? C_ENTITY_TYPEDEF
017198:                                                     : C_ENTITY_OBJECT,
017199:             .is_definition = declaration->is_definition,
017200:             .is_thread_local = is_thread_local,
017201:             .is_constexpr = declaration->is_constexpr,
017202:         };
017203:         // The name is that token's spelling, so its interned id is the
017204:         // entity's; a declaration without a name token interns the empty
017205:         // name as before.
017206:         c_parse_scope_add_entity(&result,
017207:                                  (CScopeId){
017208:                                      .value = 0,
017209:                                  },
017210:                                  entity, declaration_name_token < token_count ? preprocess.tokens[declaration_name_token].symbol : 0);
017211:     }
017212:     if (result.enum_member_count)
017213:     {
017214:         CTypeId enum_integer_type = c_parse_add_type(&result, (CType){
017215:                                                                   .element_type = C_TYPE_ID_INVALID,
017216:                                                                   .return_type = C_TYPE_ID_INVALID,
017217:                                                                   .array_bound = C_ARRAY_BOUND_INVALID,
017218:                                                                   .kind = C_TYPE_INT,
017219:                                                                   .is_complete = true,
017220:                                                               });
017221:         for (u32 member_index = 0; member_index < result.enum_member_count; member_index += 1)
017222:         {
017223:             CEnumMember* member = &result.enum_members[member_index];
017224:             u32 member_symbol = c_parse_symbol_or_intern(&result, member->symbol, member->name);
017225:             if (c_parse_lookup_entity_symbol(&result,
017226:                                              (CScopeId){
017227:                                                  .value = 0,
017228:                                              },
017229:                                              member_symbol, member->name)
017230:                     .value != C_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
017231:             {
017232:                 c_parse_diagnostic(&result, member->location, C_DIAGNOSTIC_REDEFINITION, S8("redefinition of enumerator"));
017233:                 continue;
017234:             }
017235:             CEntityId entity = {
017236:                 .value = result.entity_count,
017237:             };
017238:             BUSTER_VALIDATE(result.entity_count < result.entity_capacity);
017239:             result.entities[result.entity_count++] = (CEntity){
017240:                 .name = member->name,
017241:                 .location = member->location,
017242:                 .type = enum_integer_type,
017243:                 .scope =
017244:                     {
